Subject: Encryption & KMS options for PII data - next steps

Hi Elena/Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand Finera's ingestion patterns and the need to lock down PII processing for the payments workflow. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps: 

Recap:
- Data scope: payment-related PII (names, card last4, account IDs) flowing through the inference pipeline.
- Retention: you prefer a short retention window on logs (30–90 days) and ability to purge specific records on demand.
- Logging: need audit logs for access and token-level tracing, but logs should not contain raw PII (or should be easily redacted).
- Encryption: must have TLS in-transit and AES-256 at-rest. Preference for customer-managed keys (BYOK / CMEK) and HSM-backed keys for higher assurance.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 for all API traffic and mutual TLS options for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM; support for customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) for Hosted/Dedicated, and HSM integrations for Private/on-prem deployments.
- Logging & retention: configurable retention windows, redaction hooks for PII, and exportable audit logs (S3/GCS) with strict ACLs.

Attachments: I attached our SOC2 report and a short KMS options matrix that maps deployment modes to key management and HSM capabilities.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi/Dev: schedule a technical deep-dive to walk the KMS/HSM integration pattern and retention configuration (30–45m).
2) Finera: confirm whether BYOK (customer-managed keys) is a hard requirement for pilot or if using Redwood-managed CMEK is acceptable for initial testing.
3) I'll open a HubSpot deal and share a Calendly invite for the deep-dive.

If that all looks right, I'll loop in engineering and propose times.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A couple of clarifying questions before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) For BYOK: we need to understand whether Redwood will see plaintext keys at any point during rotation/onboarding. We have strict controls that keys must be generated and stored in our HSM.
2) For logs: can you confirm whether request/response logs ever include PII by default? We need assurance that logs are either redacted at ingest or never capture raw PII.
3) For retention/purge: can Redwood support targeted deletion (e.g., delete all records tied to an account ID) and provide proof of deletion (audit trail)?

If you can have engineering comment on those three items that would be great.

Hi Tom/Elena — quick technical answers to the three asks: 

1) BYOK / key custody:
- We support customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK) across hosted and dedicated deployments using cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- Redwood does NOT store customer key material in plaintext. For cloud KMS we use envelope encryption: your KMS performs master key operations; Redwood holds only encrypted data keys in our vault and cannot decrypt without KMS access.
- For the highest assurance, Private/on-prem deployments can integrate directly with your HSM (PKCS#11) so key material never leaves your boundary.

2) Logging and PII: 
- By default, our application logs capture metadata (request IDs, token counts, model version, latency) and NOT request/response payloads that contain PII.
- We provide redaction hooks and a client-side SDK filter so you can strip or hash PII before it reaches Redwood.
- Audit logs are available for access events (who/when) and can be exported to your storage with the retention policy you choose.

3) Retention & targeted deletion: 
- Retention windows are configurable per-route (e.g., 30/90/365 days).
- We support targeted deletion APIs that accept identifiers (account ID, request ID) and return an audit token proving deletion.
- Deletions are recorded in an immutable audit log (tamper-evident) suitable for compliance evidence.

Additional notes:
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 enforced. Mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM and envelope encryption with CMEK options.
- HSM integrations: supported for Private deployments and for customers requiring FIPS-140-2/3 validated HSMs.

Happy to walk through a diagram in the deep-dive — I can show keyflow, where encrypted data keys live, and the steps for rotation and revocation. How does tomorrow morning (11/25) or Thursday look for a 45m slot?

Thanks,
